region.text: Livonia not occupied by Russia in 1561: Vidzeme and the Pernau district; Riga a free city, Ösel Danish, Estonia Swedish

ledger.note: 28 November 1561: the Treaty of Vilnius creates the Duchy of Livonia. 'The Livonian nobility accept the Grand Duke's suzerainty in exchange for guarantees of their privileges' after the Livonian Confederation dissolved in the Livonian War.

region.text: Dorpat (Tartu) and Fellin (Viljandi), held by Russia

ledger.note: 1561: Russia holds Dorpat and Fellin inside the new duchy. The Livonian War page has Russia taking Dorpat and Narva in 1558 and Fellin in 1559-1560; the contest is dated from the duchy's birth because the page gives no later Russian advance into the duchy's land. (Magnus's Russian-backed Kingdom of Livonia, declared 1570, is a separate state that needs a dossier.)
1566: declared a duchy under a Treaty of Union between Livonian landowners and Lithuanian authorities; Jan Chodkiewicz becomes the first governor (1566-1578), seat Sigulda Castle.
1569: after the Union of Lublin the duchy becomes a joint domain of the Polish Crown and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania; 'it had been a Lithuanian province until then'. Same state, same colour.

1581: Riga comes under the Commonwealth. Riga 'for twenty years had the status of a Free Imperial City', and 'came under the influence of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth by the Treaty of Drohiczyn, which ended the war for Riga in 1581'; the Livonian War page notes the treaty reduced Riga's privileges. Whether Riga was then part of the duchy proper is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Dorpat (Tartu) and Fellin (Viljandi), held by Russia

ledger.note: 1582: the Truce of Jam Zapolski gives Dorpat and Livonia to Poland-Lithuania. 'Russia gave up its Livonian holdings and Dorpat to Poland-Lithuania'; the page gives no day.

region.text: Dorpat (Tartu) and Fellin (Viljandi), held by Russia

ledger.note: 1582: the contest with Russia over Dorpat and Fellin ends with the truce.

region.text: Livonia without Ösel: Vidzeme, Riga and southern Estonia (Dorpat, Fellin, Pernau)

ledger.note: 1600: Sweden invades Livonia. 'Sweden took control of Estonia and most of Livonia'; Chodkiewicz and Radziwiłł beat the Swedes at Kokenhusen in early 1601, Zamoyski took Wolmar and Fellin; by 1602 the Swedes held only Reval, Pernau, Hapsal and Dorpat; Dorpat surrendered in April 1603 (the page also says 1604); Kircholm 27 September 1605; Mansfeld took Daugavgriva, Fellin and Koknese in 1608 and Chodkiewicz recovered Pernau in 1609.

region.text: Livonia without Ösel: Vidzeme, Riga and southern Estonia (Dorpat, Fellin, Pernau)

ledger.note: 1611: a truce after the death of Charles IX ends the war; the infobox gives 'status quo ante bellum'. The page says the truce lasted to 1617 (or November 1620 in other sources).

region.text: Livonia without Ösel: Vidzeme, Riga and southern Estonia (Dorpat, Fellin, Pernau)

ledger.note: August 1621: Gustavus Adolphus's Swedes invade Livonia; the siege of Riga begins on 29 August.

region.text: Riga and the outlying fortress of Daugavgriva

ledger.note: 25 September 1621: Riga capitulates to Sweden. 'Riga capitulated on 25 September' after three assaults; Dünamünde fell on 2 October 1621.

region.text: Valmiera (Wolmar) and the smaller castles taken in January 1622

ledger.note: January 1622: Valmiera (Wolmar) and several smaller Livonian castles fall to the Swedes. The truce signed at Mitau on 10 August 1622 left Sweden holding them.
1625: Koknese falls to the Swedes after a sixteen-day siege (landing in June 1625).
27 August 1625: Dorpat (Tartu) falls to the Swedes.

wars.outcome: Sweden took Riga (25 September 1621), Valmiera (January 1622), Dorpat (27 August 1625) and Koknese (1625) and kept Riga and Livonia north of the Daugava; the Truce of Altmark of 25 September 1629 recognised the gains.
wars.note: The page gives two dates for the Truce of Mitau, 10 August 1622 and November 1622; the Truce of Altmark and the 1626-1629 fighting are not on this page.

certainty.note: Drawn from county and commune names; no page gives a boundary line or an area. The line against Russian-held Dorpat and Fellin before 1582 and the Swedish gains of 1622-1625 are approximate. The Inflanty (Latgale) border of 1629 is the treaty line but the page names the region only.

notes: Six pages opened against a 2-5 page budget (Swedish Livonia is shared with the swedish-livonia dossier and used here only for the successors' extent). Cliopatria has no row: the Livonian Conference row ends in 1563 and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth row starts in 1572, so the shapes 1561-1629 are all new. The Commonwealth's Cliopatria shapes from 1572 probably already contain Livonia; the renderer should draw this duchy as a vassal tint of the Commonwealth (the duchy page: 'semi-autonomous vassal state' of Lithuania, and from 1569 of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth), not as a rival colour. Shapes are the researcher's reading of county and commune names: the Duchy page gives no boundary and no area. Disagreements on the pages: the Swedish conquest is dated 1621-1625 (body), 1620-1622 (infobox) and 1600-1629 (lead) on the Duchy page; the Truce of Mitau is 10 August 1622 or November 1622; Dorpat's recapture is April 1603 or 1604. Not opened: Treaty of Drohiczyn, Truce of Altmark, Kingdom of Livonia (Magnus, 1570-1578; needs a dossier if it is to be drawn: eu-14-g also asked for it), the 1626-1629 war. Counterpart 'riga' (Free Imperial City of Riga 1561-1581) has no dossier. The Duchy of Courland and Semigallia is another state (duchy-of-courland, eu-14-h). Region names used that the gazetteer lacks: none (Valmiera is a circle by coordinates; the 'Kokneses' admin1 exists). Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): the region {admin1: Riga, country: Latvia} resolved to the whole Riga planning region (30 municipalities, about 13,150 km2), not the city; replaced by a circle round the city (8 km for the 1581 gain of the city, 10 km for Riga with Daugavgriva from 1621). Capital from 1582; kingdom-of-denmark (a row ending 1406) replaced by denmark-norway in the Livonian War.
